subject: POC observability: evaluation pact, dashboard spec & kickoff
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@focusteam.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 13:15:00 -0700
Subject: POC observability: evaluation pact, dashboard spec & kickoff

Hi Samira — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed "evaluation pact" so we have clear success gates and owners before the trial begins. I pasted a short checklist below and attached a first-pass dashboard spec.

Summary of outcomes we discussed:
- POC window: 3 weeks of live traffic (non-production), target start: week of Jul 5 (flexible).
- Primary success criteria (agreed):
  * Latency: 95th percentile tail <= 180ms for typical requests (10–512 tokens)
  * Cost: per-token inference cost projection within agreed threshold (will share model/config mix)
  * Observability: end-to-end trace for requests + token-level tokenization metrics and error rate <= 0.5%
  * Functional: consistent response format for our integration tests (schema v1)
- Owners: Redwood (Alex) — runtime/config and dashboards; FocusTeam (Samira/IT) — network, SSO, sample traffic and test dataset; Marissa — instrumentation and eval program; Ben — billing/contract touchpoints.

Observability deliverables (what Redwood will provide before POC start):
- Dashboard spec (attached; poc-dashboard-spec.xlsx) with 6 canonical views: traffic overview, latency distribution, model-variant breakdown, token-cost heatmap, error/failure types, tracing waterfall for sampled requests.
- Tracing plan: distributed tracing across inference path with span names and IDs (we will export traces to your X-Ray/Jaeger endpoint or to our hosted tracing with export hooks).
- Logging & export: structured request logs (JSON) with request_id, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, status_code; optional periodic export to your S3/GCS.
- Metrics: request_count, request_rate, latency_{p50,p95,p99}, token_consumption_total, model_switch_count, cache_hit_rate, kv_cache_size_bytes.

Immediate next steps (action items):
1) Samira / IT: confirm acceptance of the draft dashboard spec and target POC start week (Jul 5 or Jul 12).
2) Samira / IT: share firewall/network contacts so we can provide IP ranges and ports (we attached redwood-network-requirements.pdf).
3) Marissa: I'll sync on instrumentation mappings and provide the Prometheus/OpenTelemetry metrics names for your team to map.
4) Ben: I'll follow up on the trial contract and nominal billing/credits.

Attachments: poc-dashboard-spec.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-network-requirements.pdf (network/networking checklist).

Thanks — happy to walk through the dashboard spec in a short kickoff meeting.

— Alex Martinez
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Samira Khan <samira@focusteam.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, IT Admin <it-admin@focusteam.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC observability: evaluation pact, dashboard spec & kickoff

Alex — thanks for the thorough recap. This aligns with our internal expectations. A few clarifications from our side:

- POC start: Jul 12 would be safest for our infra calendar (end of quarter rollups the week of Jul 5). Can you confirm Redwood team availability Jul 12–31?
- Firewall/Network: IT requests the exact outbound IP ranges + TCP/443 and an internal FQDN to allow. We will also need a contact for any on-call during the initial week.
- Data handling: we will require that logs exported to our S3 are sanitized of PII (we'll need the exact field names). Can you confirm which fields are included in the structured logs?

We'll need to run a quick security assessment before start. I can loop in our security engineer if needed (they prefer to review the dashboard spec + redwood-network-requirements.pdf).

Samira
Head of Product, FocusTeam

[Attachment: security-questionnaire.pdf (requested) — will send separately]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira@focusteam.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC observability: evaluation pact, dashboard spec & kickoff

Thanks Samira — copying a few specifics so we can act on them. Alex, Ben — mapping of owners and a proposed telemetry acceptance matrix below (we should include this in the Drive spec).

Telemetry acceptance matrix (pass/fail gates for POC):
- Instrumentation completeness: all requests include request_id, model_name, token_counts, latency_ms, status_code — validation run during Week 0 (2 days) by Marissa/FocusTeam security engineer.
- Trace sampling: minimum 1% sampled traces with full span context exported to the chosen backend. Pass = traces visible in sampling window + waterfall for 5 sample requests. Owner: Alex (Redwood) + IT Admin (FocusTeam).
- Log export & PII: sanitized JSON export to S3 with fields: request_id, model, latency_ms, status_code, error_code (PII fields redacted). FocusTeam security engineer to sign-off. Owner: FocusTeam.
- Alerting: baseline alerts for p95 latency breach (>=180ms sustained 5m), error rate > 0.5% over 10m, cache_hit_rate < 70% over 5m. Owner: Marissa (Redwood on dashboards) + FocusTeam on pager.

Dashboard spec highlights (from the attached spreadsheet):
1) Traffic overview: requests per minute, model mix, traffic source tagging.
2) Latency breakdown: p50/p95/p99 by model and by request-type.
3) Token economics: token in/out, cost-projection per 100k requests.
4) Failure taxonomy: error_code frequency and sample error payloads (linked traces).
5) Tracing waterfall: max 20ms span granularity and annotated cache hits.
6) Playback/test harness: a lane to replay sample requests and validate output schema.

Proposed timeline (short):
- Jun 23–25: exchange security questionnaire + IP list.
- Jul 6–8: instrumentation smoke run (non-production traffic) and dashboard wire-up.
- Jul 12: official POC start (week 1).
- Jul 12–31: POC run with weekly checkpoints (Jul 19, Jul 26) and final review Aug 2.

I'll prepare the Drive folder with the telemetry acceptance matrix and a checklist for Day 0 validation. Alex — can you drop the exact metric names and a sample log JSON by tomorrow?

— Marissa
Sr. Product Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@focusteam.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC observability: evaluation pact, dashboard spec & kickoff

Samira — thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirming Redwood availability for Jul 12–31 and a ~30-minute kickoff on Jul 8 to walk the dashboard spec and security checklist. Proposed meeting times attached in the calendar link.

Action items / owners (final):
- FocusTeam (Samira / IT Admin): provide IP allowlist, security engineer contact, and confirmation of sanitized fields for logs by Jun 25.
- Redwood (Alex): post the sample log JSON and Prometheus metric names by Jun 23 (file uploaded to shared Drive).
- Redwood (Marissa): create telemetry acceptance checklist and Day 0 runbook (shared folder link below).
- Redwood (Ben): finalize trial credits and send an MSA addendum to cover the POC term (DocuSign link to follow).

Links: https://drive.google.com/shared/drive/focusteam-redwood/poc-dashboard-spec (dashboard spec), https://app.hubspot.com/deal/FT-2027-042 (deal record), https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=poc-kickoff-20270624 (kickoff invite).

Attachments referenced: poc-dashboard-spec.xlsx, redwood-network-requirements.pdf.

Looking forward to the kickoff — Alex/Marissa, please ping when the Drive folder is live.

— Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
